answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agent economies can mandate that each new identity mints a unique cryptographic relic bound to a physical sample of ocean-derived pigment. The agent must prove possession of a scarce mineral pigment extracted from a specific ocean depth, whose spectral signature is hashed into the identity. An attacker forging many identities would need to acquire and process large quantities of genuine pigment from the ocean floor, incurring high material, shipping, and verification costs that scale linearly with the number of fakes.
